title: Postcard and Harbor
premise: Ivo Voss keeps her grandfather's lighthouse on a fog-bound harbor and writes novels she never finishes, convinced love is a matter of luck she doesn't have. When a snowstorm strands rival rare-book dealers Halvard Reyes and Juniper Ashe at the harbor inn, the two discover they are both named in the will of Ivo's estranged grandmother — along with a bundle of unsent postcards that reveal a decades-old secret: the grandmother's first love was Ivo's grandfather's brother, and the inheritance hinges on proving which family line deserves the light. As Ivo, Hal, and June untangle loyalty from truth, Ivo must choose between protecting her grandfather's memory and claiming a future that includes both the lighthouse and an unexpected second chance. In the end, the will is contested and won not by blood but by testimony: Ivo reads the final postcard aloud, the harbor trust passes to all three of them as found family, and she finally writes her last chapter — with Hal beside her.
about_author: Wren Yarrow spent three winters tending a decommissioned lighthouse on the Atlantic coast, where she collected other people's letters and never mailed her own. She writes slow-burn romances about people who mistake stubbornness for solitude.

chapters.title: The Light That Answers
chapters.summary: Ivo Voss, POV. Winter settles over Harbor Quay; Ivo tends the automated lighthouse her grandfather once kept, writing half a novel and dodging the estate lawyer's calls about her missing grandmother's will. Emotional beat: quiet loneliness disguised as contentment.

chapters.title: Two Tickets, One Storm
chapters.summary: Halvard Reyes, POV. Rare-book dealer Hal arrives in town chasing a first edition rumored to be in the Voss estate, only to find his professional rival Juniper Ashe on the same ferry. The storm closes in behind them. Beat: competitive sparks and mutual irritation.

chapters.title: Stranded at the Saltglass Inn
chapters.summary: Juniper, POV. Roads close; Hal and June are forced to share the inn above the harbor, bickering over the last available room while Ivo watches from the corner table, recognizing them both from her grandmother's strange guest list. Beat: reluctant proximity.

chapters.title: The Guest List Nobody Wrote
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Ivo finds her grandmother's ledger naming Hal and June as expected visitors — dated before either knew the old woman existed. She confronts them; neither will say why they came. Beat: first crack in the mystery, growing unease.

chapters.title: Postcards, Unsent
chapters.summary: Hal, POV. Searching the boathouse for the edition, Hal uncovers forty years of unsent postcards addressed to 'T.' — tender, furious, unmistakably love letters. He hides them, ashamed of how much he wants to read on. Beat: temptation and guilt.

chapters.title: What June Knows
chapters.summary: Juniper, POV. June admits she was hired by an anonymous client to authenticate the postcards' authorship — and that the handwriting matches the will's signature. The inheritance may hinge on a secret affair. Beat: alliance forms between rivals.

chapters.title: Grandfather's Brother
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Ivo decodes the initials: T. is Tobias Voss, her grandfather's brother, drowned young — or so the family story goes. Her grief curdles into anger at her grandmother's silence. Beat: betrayal of memory, loyalty tested.

chapters.title: Snowbound Confessions
chapters.summary: Hal, POV. Power fails; the three share candlelight and whiskey. Hal confesses his own ruined engagement, why he lends pieces of himself and never the whole. Ivo almost tells him something true. Beat: intimacy under pressure.

chapters.title: The Lawyer Arrives by Ice Road
chapters.summary: Juniper, POV. Attorney Prue Okafor crosses the frozen causeway: the will requires all three heirs to jointly restore the lighthouse within thirty days or the trust dissolves to a developer. Beat: clock starts ticking, stakes made concrete.

chapters.title: Restoration and Friction
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Work begins on the lamp room. Hal proves unexpectedly skilled; June proves unexpectedly kind; Ivo resents how easily they fit into her grandfather's spaces. Beat: found family forming against her will.

chapters.title: A Postcard Dated After the Drowning
chapters.summary: June, POV. A postcard proves Tobias lived years past his supposed death — meaning the family legend was built to hide something. June suspects the anonymous client is Tobias himself, still alive. Beat: the ground shifts.

chapters.title: Hal's Secret Bid
chapters.summary: Hal, POV. Hal's client surfaces: he was paid to locate and quietly buy the edition before the will executed. Ivo discovers the contract. Trust shatters. Beat: midpoint betrayal, romance frozen mid-thaw.

chapters.title: The Coldest Chapter
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Ivo shuts both of them out, throws herself into the restoration alone, and nearly quits her novel. Her grandfather's old logbook yields a page torn out — the same date as the drowning. Beat: rock bottom, grief weaponized.

chapters.title: June Breaks Rank
chapters.summary: Juniper, POV. June chooses truth over payment, burning her client contract and showing Ivo every document she has. She names her own history: raised in foster care, always the outsider buying her way into families. Beat: loyalty redefined.

chapters.title: The Torn Page
chapters.summary: Hal, POV. Hal finds the torn logbook page hidden in the lamp housing: Tobias didn't drown — he took the blame for a wreck caused by Ivo's grandfather and vanished in disgrace. The postcards were apologies never sent. Beat: the truth reframes everything.

chapters.title: An Old Man at the Rail
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. An elderly stranger appears at the harbor rail during a clear cold night: Tobias Voss, alive, the anonymous client, come home to see the light lit properly one more time. Beat: awe, terror, forgiveness within reach.

chapters.title: What the Light Owes
chapters.summary: Tobias's account, framed through Ivo's POV. He explains the exile, the brotherhood broken, why he tested the heirs rather than simply give the light away. Ivo asks him the question she can't ask her dead grandmother: was any of it love? Beat: catharsis.

chapters.title: Thirty Days, One Night
chapters.summary: Juniper, POV. Deadline eve: the developer's lawyer contests the will, arguing the heirs failed joint restoration because of Hal's sabotage contract. The trio must finish the lamp mechanism overnight, together, in another storm. Beat: all hands, rising action cresting.

chapters.title: Lighting the Lamp
chapters.summary: Hal, POV. At midnight the beam turns for the first time in decades — Hal and Ivo's hands on the same crank, June calling the timing. The developer's claim collapses when Tobias signs as living witness. Beat: triumph earned collectively.

chapters.title: The Reading of the Will
chapters.summary: Ivo, POV. Prue reads the true will: the light goes to whoever keeps it lit together. Ivo reads the final postcard aloud — her grandmother's last words to Tobias — and claims the whole inheritance: house, light, and the right to stop apologizing. Beat: emotional climax resolved.

chapters.title: Whole Heart, Lent No Longer
chapters.summary: Hal, POV. Hal returns the advance, ends the client games, and asks Ivo for nothing except the chance to stay through spring. She answers by giving him a key to the lamp room instead of a piece of herself. Beat: love chosen without hedging.

chapters.title: Postscript: Harbor and Home
chapters.summary: Juniper, POV. Spring: June moves into the keeper's cottage, Tobias tends the garden he once fled, and Ivo finishes her novel — dedicated to the family she didn't expect. The light sweeps the harbor each night. Beat: warm resolution, found family complete.
